claim: High computational and energy cost of LLMs, together with non-negligible and variable inference latency, makes end-to-end responsiveness sensitive to request frequency and workload bursts.
falsifier: Measure end-to-end latency and throughput of an LLM-based decision system under different request rates and burst patterns; compare to a system with constant low-latency inference.

conditions: when LLMs are used in online resource allocation or root-cause analysis tasks
under varying request frequency and workload bursts
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Computational and energy cost–end-to-end responsiveness boundary

claim: In the σ-mechanics formulation of Poincaré-Snyder relativity, the free particle dynamics naturally describes Einstein particles, antiparticles, tachyonic particles, and tachyonic antiparticles on the same footing.
falsifier: One can derive the equations of motion for the free particle in σ-mechanics and verify that the solutions correspond to the different particle types under the usual time evolution picture.

conditions: free particle case with Hamiltonian H = 1/2 p_μ p^μ
exclusions: limited to the free particle case in the σ-mechanics formalism as presented

title: Free particle σ-mechanics–unified description of Einstein theorem

claim: A per-residue dihedral adherence score can identify specific residues in a predicted protein structure that have high error relative to the experimentally determined structure, enabling pinpointing of areas needing improvement.
falsifier: The per-residue error identification can be tested on other proteins by computing the dihedral adherence score for each residue and comparing to known high-error regions.

exclusions: limited to the sampled system (protein 7W6B predictions) and reported experimental conditions

title: Per-residue dihedral adherence score for identification of residues
